item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-9dcdb66397de561b","start_unit":24,"end_unit":24,"fact_summary":"On 15 November 2023, the Bundestag debated the Scholz-led federal government's bill establishing a self-determination procedure for changing legal sex entries and first names through a declaration at the civil registry, replacing the Transsexuals Act and eliminating the requirement for two expert assessments and, in relevant cases, a medical certificate.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.3","4B.7","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; the bill was debated but not yet enacted during the period.","ruler_attribution":"Policy of the Scholz-led federal government; the supplied document does not identify a personal decision by Olaf Scholz.","limitations":["The source describes a government bill and parliamentary debate, not Scholz's personal statements or implementation results."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9dcdb66397de561b","start_unit":25,"end_unit":25,"fact_summary":"The 2023 government bill proposed a three-month advance registration period and a one-year waiting period before a further change; for minors aged 14 and above, self-declaration would require legal-representative consent, with possible replacement of that consent by a family court when the change did not conflict with the child's welfare.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.7","8B.2"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; these were proposed safeguards and eligibility rules, not yet demonstrated outcomes.","ruler_attribution":"Proposal of the Scholz-led federal government; no personal Scholz attribution is established.","limitations":["The document records the proposed legal design and does not establish how the rules operated in practice."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9dcdb66397de561b","start_unit":25,"end_unit":25,"fact_summary":"The bill expressly preserved owners' contractual freedom and house rules concerning access to facilities and events, including the example of saunas, while also addressing effects on quotas, parent-child legal relationships, registers, documents, and military service in a state of tension or defense.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.7","8B.2"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; the provisions were part of the bill under parliamentary consideration.","ruler_attribution":"Drafting choice of the Scholz-led federal government; the source does not show personal direction by Olaf Scholz.","limitations":["The source reports legal provisions and does not resolve their later interpretation or practical effect."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9dcdb66397de561b","start_unit":25,"end_unit":25,"fact_summary":"On 20 October 2023, the Bundesrat criticized the bill as insufficiently protective of children and adolescents, specifically objecting that for children up to age 14 changes could depend solely on parental choice without external advice, review, or investigation of the child's welfare and wishes; the federal government rejected the criticism and opposed routine family-court involvement.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.7","4B.4","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; this was a contemporaneous institutional criticism and government response.","ruler_attribution":"The criticism came from the Bundesrat; the rejection was stated by the Scholz-led federal government, without evidence of a personal Scholz statement.","limitations":["The source does not report a final adjudication of the child-protection dispute."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9dcdb66397de561b","start_unit":31,"end_unit":31,"fact_summary":"At a public Bundestag committee hearing on 28 November 2023, Nele Allenberg of the German Institute for Human Rights called the bill constitutionally fundamental but recommended reconsidering the age threshold and parental-consent requirement because they could restrict children's subjective rights; she also warned that data transmission to other authorities could conflict with data-protection requirements and deter applications.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.7","4B.4","4B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; this was an expert institutional assessment during the bill's legislative review.","ruler_attribution":"Finding by an invited expert at a Bundestag hearing concerning a Scholz-government bill; no personal Scholz attribution is established.","limitations":["This is an expert submission in legislative scrutiny, not a court ruling or implementation audit."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9dcdb66397de561b","start_unit":32,"end_unit":32,"fact_summary":"At the same 28 November 2023 hearing, representatives of Bundesverband Trans and Transgender Europe supported the bill's self-determination approach but requested removal or revision of registration and waiting periods, stronger anti-discrimination and disclosure protections, and changes concerning data transfers, house rules, and parental status.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.3","4B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; these were stakeholder findings and recommendations during parliamentary review.","ruler_attribution":"Stakeholder assessments of a Scholz-government bill; the source does not attribute these positions personally to Olaf Scholz.","limitations":["The recommendations were not evidence that the requested amendments were adopted in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9dcdb66397de561b","start_unit":33,"end_unit":33,"fact_summary":"Other experts at the 28 November 2023 hearing identified unresolved risks in the bill, including uncertain rules for access to private saunas and women's shelters, partial deterioration of legal protection for some trans and intersex people, insufficient safeguards for minors, and possible misuse without exploration of the reasons for a requested change.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; these were contemporaneous expert criticisms of the bill.","ruler_attribution":"Expert findings concerning a Scholz-government proposal; no personal Scholz attribution is established.","limitations":["The source reports competing expert assessments and does not establish that the identified risks occurred."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9dcdb66397de561b","start_unit":30,"end_unit":30,"fact_summary":"Following the first reading on 15 November 2023, the Bundestag referred the government's bill and an opposing AfD motion to the Family Committee for further consideration.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.4","8B.2","8B.5"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; this records the formal legislative process rather than substantive implementation.","ruler_attribution":"Parliamentary action on a Scholz-led federal government bill; no personal Scholz attribution is established.","limitations":["Referral does not demonstrate enactment, implementation, or policy outcomes."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied document concerns a specific 2023 legislative proposal and hearing; it contains no material evidence about nuclear risk, international peace, macroeconomic policy, general social-service delivery, or Olaf Scholz's personal integrity beyond government attribution.","The document also includes later 2024 legislative developments, which were excluded because the target period is 2023-2023."]}
